topicName: Arbitrary Values and Arbitrary Properties Syntax

[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering Arbitrary Values and Arbitrary Properties Syntax in Tailwind CSS"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"While Tailwind CSS provides an extensive, highly configurable design system out of the box, you will occasionally encounter edge cases where you need a one-off value that does not map to your tailwind.config.js file. Tailwind solves this gracefully using arbitrary values and arbitrary properties syntax."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Arbitrary Values"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Arbitrary values allow you to use square brackets to pass any arbitrary CSS value directly to a utility class. Instead of being restricted to Tailwind's default spacing or color scales, you can inject exact values on the fly."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"
"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"Tailwind is smart enough to infer the CSS property based on the utility name. However, for ambiguous properties, you can explicitly provide a data type hint inside the brackets."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"
"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Arbitrary Properties Syntax"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"When you need to apply a CSS property that Tailwind does not have a dedicated utility for, or when you want to write raw CSS inline using Tailwind syntax, you can use the arbitrary properties syntax."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"
"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Handling Spaces in Arbitrary Values"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Because CSS values like grid-template-columns or box-shadow often contain spaces, and spaces are used in HTML to separate class names, you must use underscores (_) instead of spaces within your arbitrary values. Tailwind will automatically convert these underscores back to spaces during compilation."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"
"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices and Caveats"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use design tokens first: Rely on your theme configuration in tailwind.config.js for values used repeatedly across your application."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Avoid magic numbers: Arbitrary values are powerful, but overusing them can lead to inconsistent UIs just like traditional inline styles."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Combine with modifiers: Arbitrary values fully support responsive prefixes, states, and dark mode (e.g., md:top-[120px] dark:bg-[#121212])."}]
